summary.text: Janelle Bynum is the Democratic nominee for re-election to Oregon's 5th Congressional District, which she has represented since January 2025. An electrical engineer and MBA who became a McDonald's franchise owner in Clackamas County, she served eight years in the Oregon House of Representatives, including as chair of the Committee on Small Business and Economic Development. In Congress she serves on the Financial Services Committee.

paragraphs.text: Bynum was born in 1975 and grew up in Washington, D.C., where she attended Banneker High School and graduated from The Madeira School.
She earned a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from Florida A&M University in 1996 and an MBA from the University of Michigan's Ross School of Business in 2000.

She worked as an engineer, including as a steering systems engineer at General Motors. In 2002 she moved to Clackamas County, Oregon, to help run a McDonald's franchise, and she became a franchise owner.

Bynum won an Oregon House seat (District 51) in 2016, defeating Republican Lori Chavez-DeRemer, then the mayor of Happy Valley. She was re-elected in 2018, 2020 and 2022 (in District 39 after redistricting) and served eight years, from 2017 to 2025.

In the Oregon House she chaired the Committee on Small Business and Economic Development. Her office says she led efforts that added $43 billion and more than 6,000 jobs to Oregon's economy, and she was chief sponsor of the 2023 Oregon CHIPS Act, a $210 million semiconductor industry initiative.
Bynum was elected to Congress on November 5, 2024, defeating incumbent Republican Lori Chavez-DeRemer, and was sworn in in January 2025.

She serves on the House Financial Services Committee, including its Subcommittees on Housing and Insurance and on Capital Markets and the Task Force on Monetary Policy, Treasury Market Resilience, and Economic Prosperity. She is a member of caucuses including the Congressional Black Caucus, Labor Caucus and Extreme Heat Caucus.

She has volunteered with the Ronald McDonald House Charities of Oregon board, Business Oregon, the Center for Women's Leadership, and the Oregon Commission on Black Affairs. According to her office, she is the daughter of teachers and a mother of four who lives in Happy Valley with her husband Mark.
